hindi: दोनों अंस यानी कन्धों में आठ।
english: Eight in the two shoulders (aṃsa).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units. GROUPING: appears to continue the snāyu counts of u156-172 (the preceding unit run ends at u172). Counts are translated as printed. Sandhi aṣṭau + aṃsayoḥ = aṣṭāvaṃsayoḥ.

words.gloss: manyā (side of the neck; probable); avaṭu (hollow at the nape; probable); eye; lip; palate

hindi: मन्या यानी सम्भवतः गर्दन का पार्श्व, अवटु यानी सम्भवतः गर्दन के पीछे का गड्ढा, नेत्र, ओष्ठ और तालु में दो-दो।
english: Two each in the manyā (probably the side of the neck), the avaṭu (probably the hollow at the nape), the eyes (netra), the lips (oṣṭha) and the palate (tālu).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units. manyā and avaṭu are probable identifications only (both words have also been read as parts of the nape/neck; not certain). The avagraha printed after -ā in manyā'vaṭu is a print habit, not an elision. The Sanskrit does not say whether each of the five sites has two for each side.

hindi: ग्रीवा यानी गर्दन में तीस।
english: Thirty in the neck (grīvā).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: जत्रु यानी हँसली में तीन।
english: Three in the jatru (collar-bone).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units. jatruṇi is read as locative singular of jatru (n.); a dual (jatrvoḥ, as in u120) would be expected for the two collar-bones, so the number of the noun is uncertain (the form could also be taken as a neuter plural jatrūṇi with a short vowel). Count is as printed.

hindi: हनु यानी दोनों जबड़ों में चार।
english: Four in the two jaws (hanu).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units. Printed 'catvārihanvoḥ' is two words run together (catvāri hanvoḥ); no sandhi is involved.

hindi: जिह्वा यानी जीभ में पाँच।
english: Five in the tongue (jihvā).

text_flags.why: variant spelling jivhā for jihvā (h/v letter reversal, seen elsewhere in this print); normalised to jihvā in `words`, recorded once book-wide.

notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: ऊपर और नीचे के दन्तमांस यानी मसूड़ों में बारह।
english: Twelve in the upper and lower gums (dantamāṃsa, literally tooth-flesh).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units. Token dvādaśottarādhareṣu = dvādaśa + uttara-adhareṣu (a + u > o). The adjectives uttara and adhara agree with the following locative plural.

hindi: मूर्धा यानी सिर में छह।
english: Six in the head (mūrdhan).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units. Printed ṣaṇmūrddhani = ṣaṭ mūrdhani (ṭ + m > ṇm); doubled -rdd- is a print habit (mūrdhani), normalised in `words`.

hindi: उनमें अंगों और सन्धियों में रहने वाले प्रतानयुक्त यानी लता की शाखाओं या तन्तुओं वाले हैं।
english: Among these, (ones) in the limbs and in the joints are tendrilled (pratānavat, having spreading branches).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units. Copula understood. 'Among these' for tatra is the natural reading; 'there' is the plain meaning. pratāna = tendril, creeper-shoot; the Sanskrit gives no comparison with a creeper, so none is added.

words.gloss: large; sinews (snāva; probably ligaments or tendons, probable)

hindi: पर जो बड़े स्नायु यानी सम्भवतः लिगामेंट या टेंडन गोल हैं, वे कण्डरा यानी सम्भवतः टेंडन नाम वाले हैं।
english: But the large sinews (snāva; probably ligaments or tendons) that are round, those are called kaṇḍarā (probably tendons).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units. Printed 'vṛttānitāni' = vṛttāni tāni (two words run together). snāva is used as a variant of snāyu. Copula understood. kaṇḍarā = tendon is probable.

words.gloss: bladder (basti, standard); seat of the raw (āma) and of the cooked (pakva): āmāśaya and pakvāśaya, probably the stomach and the large intestine (probable); intestines (antra)

hindi: बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय, कच्चे और पके के स्थान यानी आमाशय और पक्वाशय जो सम्भवतः पेट और बड़ी आँत हैं, तथा आँतों में खोखले।
english: Hollow (ones) in the bladder (basti), in the seats of the raw and the cooked (āmāśaya and pakvāśaya, probably the stomach and the large intestine) and in the intestines (antra).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units. bastyāmapakvāśayāntreṣu is read basti + āma-pakva-āśaya + antra; āmapakvāśaya may be a contracted dvandva for āmāśaya and pakvāśaya, which is why the translation names both. basti = bladder here (cf. u168).

hindi: पार्श्वों, पीठ, छाती और सिर में चौड़े।
english: Broad (ones) in the sides (pārśva), the back (pṛṣṭha), the chest (uras) and the head (śiras).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (snāyu, from the run of counts begun at u156) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: क्योंकि स्नायु के बन्धनों से सन्धियों में भली-भाँति बँधा शरीर नाव की तरह ठीक से चेष्टा करता है।
english: For the body, well bound in the joints by the bonds of sinew (snāva), acts properly, like a boat.

text_flags.why: possible: samyak + īhate gives samyagīhate; the printed doubled g (gg) looks like a print slip.

notes: īhate is √īh 'strive, act, move'; 'acts properly' is chosen, 'moves well' is the alternative. Subject tanu (f., body) and the simile nau agree with subaddhā.

words.gloss: bone; vessel (sirā; probable); and so on

hindi: इसलिए हड्डी, सिरा आदि से भी अधिक उनकी यत्न से रक्षा करनी चाहिए।
english: Therefore one should protect them with effort, even more than the bones (asthi), the vessels (sirā) and the rest.
notes: 'More than' renders the ablative of comparison with api; the alternative reading 'protect them even from (injury to) the bones, vessels etc.' is less natural. tāni = the sinews of the preceding units. sirā = vessel (probable).

hindi: और जो बाहरी और भीतरी स्नायुओं को भली-भाँति जानता है, वह छिपे हुए शल्य यानी शरीर में घुसी बाहरी वस्तु को भी निकालने में समर्थ होता है।
english: And he who knows well the sinews (snāva), external and internal, becomes able to extract even a hidden śalya (foreign body).
notes: Printed āharttum has a doubled -rtt-, normalised to āhartum in `words`. śalya = foreign body, dart, splinter (standard).

hindi: पाँच सौ पेशियाँ यानी मांसपेशियाँ।
english: Five hundred peśī (muscles).
notes: GROUPING: appears to begin a new enumeration (muscles) after the snāyu counts of u156-187. Copula understood; the Sanskrit has no verb. peśī is also the word for a flesh-lump elsewhere (e.g. embryology); here it is read as muscle.

hindi: उनमें से चार सौ शाखाओं यानी हाथ-पैरों में।
english: Of these, four hundred in the limbs (śākhā).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. Printed 'catvāriśatāni' = catvāri śatāni (two words run together).

hindi: अन्तराधि यानी धड़ में साठ।
english: Sixty in the trunk (antarādhi).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: ऊपर चालीस।
english: Forty above.
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. ūrdhvam is read as the part of the body above the trunk, matching ūrdhvam saptatiḥ in u159; the Sanskrit itself says only 'above'.

words.gloss: in the leg (sakthi; lower limb, thigh)

hindi: वहाँ प्रत्येक सक्थि यानी निचले अंग में, पाँव की हर अँगुली में तीन।
english: There, in each single leg (sakthi, lower limb), three in each toe.
notes: Sandhi tatra + ekaikasmin = tatraikaikasmin. The feminine tisraḥ shows the counted items are feminine (peśyaḥ). sakthi may mean thigh or the whole lower limb; 'lower limb' is chosen because the toes are counted under it.

hindi: वे पन्द्रह हैं।
english: Those are fifteen.
notes: Copula understood. The Sanskrit does not give the arithmetic; fifteen is as printed.

words.gloss: in the forepart of the foot (prapada, standard)
in the sole of the foot

hindi: प्रपद यानी पैर के अगले भाग, पादतल यानी तलवे और गुल्फ यानी टखने में दस-दस।
english: Ten each in the prapada (forepart of the foot), the sole of the foot (pādatala) and the ankle (gulpha).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. Doubled daśa daśa is distributive 'ten each'; it is not stated whether the ten each is per leg (carried from u192).

words.gloss: in the kūrma (tortoise; here probably a tortoise-shaped part of the foot, probable)

hindi: वैसे ही पैर के ऊपर कूर्म में स्थित; कूर्म यानी सम्भवतः पैर का कछुए की पीठ के आकार का ऊपरी भाग।
english: Likewise, (ones) situated above the foot, in the kūrma (probably a tortoise-shaped part of the foot).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. No numeral is printed in this unit; none is supplied (the daśa daśa of u194 may carry, or a numeral may have dropped). The printed kūrmme has a doubled mm, normalised to kūrma. kūrma as a part of the foot is probable only.

hindi: जंघा यानी घुटने के नीचे की पिंडली में बीस।
english: Twenty in the jaṅghā (lower leg, calf).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. Hindi जंघा alone usually means thigh; the glossed sense here is the leg below the knee.

hindi: जानु यानी घुटने में पाँच।
english: Five in the knee (jānu).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: ऊरु यानी जाँघ में बीस।
english: Twenty in the thigh (ūru).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. The printed Devanagari of this line (विंशतिरू्रौ) is garbled, but the IAST reads viṃśatirūrau = viṃśatiḥ ūrau without difficulty.

words.gloss: penis (meṇḍra, variant of meḍhra, standard); sevanī (seam, raphe; probable)

hindi: मेण्ड्र यानी लिंग और सेवनी यानी सम्भवतः सीवन अर्थात् मध्य रेखा में एक-एक।
english: One each in the meṇḍra (penis) and the sevanī (probably the seam, the raphe).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. meṇḍra is kept as printed (also u168); it is a variant of meḍhra. sevanī as the raphe is probable only. The Sanskrit has the dual because two sites are named.

hindi: दोनों वृषण यानी अण्ड-ग्रन्थियों में दो।
english: Two in the two testicles (vṛṣaṇa).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: स्फिज् यानी दोनों नितम्बों में दस।
english: Ten in the two buttocks (sphij).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: गुद यानी मलद्वार में तीन; परन्तु वे वली यानी सिलवट नाम वाली हैं।
english: Three in the anus (guda); but those are called valī (folds).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. Sandhi tisraḥ + gude = tisro gude; tāḥ + tu = tāstu. valī (v/b spellings interchange in this print) = fold, wrinkle.

hindi: बस्ति के शिर यानी मूत्राशय के सिर में दो।
english: Two in the head of the bladder (bastiśiras).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. bastiśiras is kept literal ('head of the bladder'); its exact part is not stated.

hindi: उदर यानी पेट में चार।
english: Four in the belly (udara).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. catasra udare is regular sandhi for catasraḥ udare.

hindi: नाभि में एक।
english: One in the navel (nābhi).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: हृदय और आमाशय यानी पेट में दो।
english: Two in the heart (hṛd) and in the stomach (āmāśaya).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. Printed 'āmāśayeca' = āmāśaye ca (run together). It is not stated whether the two are for each site or in all.

words.gloss: liver (yakṛt, standard); spleen (plīha, standard); uṇḍuka (caecum; probable)

hindi: यकृत् यानी जिगर, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली और उण्डुक यानी सम्भवतः अन्धान्त्र में छह।
english: Six in the liver (yakṛt), the spleen (plīhan) and the uṇḍuka (probably the caecum).

text_flags.why: possible: the standard word is uṇḍuka (retroflex ṇḍ); the print has dental nd. Corrected in `words`.

notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. plīha + uṇḍuka gives plīhoṇḍuka (a + u > o). uṇḍuka = caecum is probable only; the exact part is not stated.

hindi: पीठ में पाँच, ऊपर की ओर स्थित।
english: Five in the back (pṛṣṭha), set upward.

text_flags.why: missing doubled n: sam-ni-viṣṭa gives sanniviṣṭa (cf. sanniviṣṭāḥ, u195); saniviṣṭa is not a word.

notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. ūrdhva could be 'upward' (running up) or 'above'; 'set upward' is the literal rendering.

hindi: दोनों पार्श्वों यानी बगलों में दस लम्बी।
english: Ten long (ones) in the two sides (pārśva).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. Printed 'dīrghāḥpārśvayoḥ' is two words run together (no sandhi).

hindi: वक्ष यानी छाती में दस।
english: Ten in the chest (vakṣas).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: अंस यानी कन्धों और अक्षक यानी सम्भवतः हँसलियों के ऊपर तीन, अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: Three above the shoulders (aṃsa) and the akṣaka (probably collar-bones), on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: asākṣaka has no sense; aṃsākṣaka (shoulders and collar-bones, cf. u119, u172-173) fits, with the anusvāra lost in print.

notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. The reading aṃsākṣaka is a conjecture; asākṣaka cannot be explained as printed. akṣaka = collar-bone is probable (u172 counts four in the two akṣaka).

hindi: ग्रीवा यानी गर्दन में दस।
english: Ten in the neck (grīvā).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: गण्ड यानी दोनों गालों में आठ।
english: Eight in the two cheeks (gaṇḍa).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units.

hindi: हनु यानी दोनों जबड़ों में आठ।
english: Eight in the two jaws (hanu).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units.

words.gloss: throat (gala, standard); kākala (uvula or laryngeal prominence; disputed); tongue; head

hindi: गला यानी कण्ठ, काकल जिसकी पहचान विवादित है यानी घण्टी या कण्ठमणि, जीभ और सिर में एक-एक।
english: One each in the gala (throat), the kākala (uvula or the laryngeal prominence; identity disputed), the tongue (jihvā) and the head (mūrdhan).
notes: ELLIPSIS: no noun or verb is printed; the counted item (peśī, introduced in u188) is carried from the preceding units. Printed jivhā is the variant spelling already recorded at u178; mūrddhasu = mūrdhasu (doubled dd).
